findings.title: Conversion Rate Decline Week-over-Week
findings.claim: Conversion rate (transactions per visitor) decreased from 0.2408 to 0.2312, a -4.0% decline. Analysis period had 1313 transactions from 5679 valid footfall counts across 7 days with operational sensors.
coverage_notes: Analysis period: 7 days with valid (non-dead-sensor) traffic data
Previous period: 7 days with valid traffic data
Dead sensor days excluded from footfall denominator
assumptions: Each unique transaction_id represents one customer sale
Door count is accurate for non-dead-sensor intervals
Conversion metric assumes all footfall is potential customer base

findings.title: Labour Cost Ratio Increase
findings.claim: Labour cost as percentage of revenue increased from 13.3% to 16.6%, a 3.4 percentage point increase. Analysis period had 7568 SAR labour cost against 45464 SAR revenue across 7 staffed days.
coverage_notes: Analysis period: 7 days with staff records
Previous period: 7 days with staff records
Revenue calculated as sum of line_total_sar for non-refund transactions
assumptions: Labour cost data is complete for staffed days
Hourly rates and shift durations are accurate
Revenue includes all payment methods and channels

findings.title: Known Waste Cost Increase
findings.claim: Known waste cost increased from 741 SAR to 1194 SAR. Waste rate (units wasted / units ordered) was 18.0% in previous period and 22.3% in analysis period, a 4.2 percentage point increase. 6 SKUs had measurable waste in analysis period.
coverage_notes: Analysis period: 6 inventory records across 6 SKUs
Previous period: 6 inventory records across 6 SKUs
Known waste cost calculated from units_wasted × unit_cost_sar
Unknown waste values excluded per data quality rules
assumptions: Inventory records represent complete weekly counts
Unit costs are accurate for waste valuation
Waste is independent of sales volume
